title: Extracts from Adam's Diary, translated from the original ms.

evidence.paraphrase: The narrator expresses annoyance at the new creature that constantly follows him.
evidence.quote: This new creature with the long hair is a good deal in the way. It is always hanging around and following me about. I don	tt like this; I am not used to company.

evidence.paraphrase: Eve investigates why carnivore-toothed animals eat plants, reasoning from their anatomy.
evidence.quote: trying to study out why the animals called lions and tigers live on grass and flowers, when, as she says, the sort of teeth they wear would indicate that they were intended to eat each other

evidence.paraphrase: The narrator notes that death has not yet entered the world.
evidence.quote: that would introduce what, as I understand it, is called 	ttdeath;	tt and death, as I have been told, has not yet entered the Park

evidence.paraphrase: After Eve eats the fruit, the animals suddenly turn violent and death enters the world.
evidence.quote: all of a sudden they broke into a tempest of frightful noises, and in one moment the plain was in a frantic commotion and every beast was destroying its neighbor. I knew what it meant	ttEve had eaten that fruit, and death was come into the world

evidence.paraphrase: As a consequence of the fall, they must now work for their living.
evidence.quote: Another thing, she says it is ordered that we work for our living hereafter. She will be useful. I will superintend.

evidence.paraphrase: The narrator tests whether the new creature is a fish by putting it in water.
evidence.quote: The difference in size warrants the conclusion that it is a different and new kind of animal	tta fish, perhaps, though when I put it in the water to see, it sank

evidence.paraphrase: The narrator classifies the child as a kangaroo variant based on its limbs, noting it is uncatalogued.
evidence.quote: The short front legs and long hind ones indicate that it is of the kangaroo family, but it is a marked variation of the species, since the true kangaroo hops, whereas this one never does. Still, it is a curious and interesting variety, and has not been catalogued before.

evidence.paraphrase: The narrator assigns a scientific-sounding species name to the creature he believes he discovered.
evidence.quote: As I discovered it, I have felt justified in securing the credit of the discovery by attaching my name to it, and hence have called it Kangaroorum Adamiensis

evidence.paraphrase: The narrator sets traps in an attempt to catch another specimen for study.
evidence.quote: I have set a dozen traps, but they do no good. I catch all small animals except that one

evidence.paraphrase: The narrator expresses frustration at being unable to classify the growing creature.
evidence.quote: I am like to lose my mind over the capricious and harassing developments of this unclassifiable zoological freak.

evidence.paraphrase: The narrator, misreading his child as a bear, plans to muzzle it while the reader knows it is a baby.
evidence.quote: Bears are dangerous	ttsince our catastrophe	ttand I shall not be satisfied to have this one prowling about the place much longer without a muzzle on.

evidence.paraphrase: The narrator interprets his talking child as a new species of bear, a gap the reader recognizes.
evidence.quote: the bear has learned to paddle around all by itself on its hind legs, and says 	ttpoppa	tt and 	ttmomma.	tt It is certainly a new species.

evidence.paraphrase: The narrator reflects that he was wrong about Eve and now values her companionship.
evidence.quote: After all these years, I see that I was mistaken about Eve in the beginning; it is better to live outside the Garden with her than inside it without her.
